newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Value of Brazil C bonds up 30 pct over dlr -report.
newsitem.headline: Value of Brazil C bonds up 30 pct over dlr -report.

text.p: The value of Brazilian foreign debt titles has risen 30 percent over the dollar so far this year, an unusually high rate of return on world markets, O Globo newspaper said.
The paper, quoting experts, said the rise in Brazil's Brady capitalization bonds, known as C-Bonds, indicates growing confidence in the Brazil's economy.
"With each passing day, Brazil gains more credibility," Morgan Stanley's Francisco Gros, a former Central Bank chief, was quoted as saying.
"There are a lot of resources in the international market looking for good investments and that also is making people take a closer look at Brazil."
The rise has prompted higher demand for Brazilian paper, extended financing terms and expectations Brazil's sovereign debt risk rating will be adjusted soon overseas, he said.
The value of Brazil C-Bonds, per dollar traded in New York, rose from $0.57375 on December 29 to $0.685 on Tuesday.
